mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary policy eases.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines for 3 months, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% in a 3-month window signals labor market deterioration that reduces corporate profit expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.0% for 3 months, or Rank IC remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate weakening housing market conditions that reduce consumer confidence and drive negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both RSAFS and HOUST decline for 2 months, or Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production declining below 105.0 indicates easing supply chain constraints that boost corporate margins, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is below 105.0, or Rank IC remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained growth in consumer spending (RSAFS) over 6 months signals strong aggregate demand that supports corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS rises for 6 months, or Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 3.5% triggers hawkish monetary policy expectations that increase real interest rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.5%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate above 4.5% combined with federal funds rate below 0.5% signals accommodative policy response to labor weakness, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 4.5% and FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Late-cycle expansion regimes defined by high RSAFS and HOUST lead to stretched valuations that cause negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods during late-cycle expansion (RSAFS > 450,000 and HOUST > 1100), or Rank IC remains below 0.03.
